Issued at 234 AM CDT Mon Sep 14 2026

Early this morning an upper level trough extended from western MT, 
southward across the Great Basin. An downstream upper level ridge 
was located across the Plains states. An upper trough was moving 
east across the eastern Greet Lakes and eastern OH River Valley.

The 6Z surface map showed a warm front extending from northwest AR 
and northeast OK, then stretched northwest across west central KS 
into eastern CO. The warm front will undergo frontolysis Today and 
reform across central NE. Isentropic lift and WAA will cause 
elevated showers and thunderstorms to develop across southern 
NE/northeast KS. 

Today through Tuesday:

The better chances for showers and elevated thunderstorms will be 
across northeast KS, though,  some isolated storms may form a bit 
farther southwest across portions of east central and north central 
KS through 12Z MON. As the warm front reforms farther north of the 
CWA later this morning the isentropic lift will shift northeast into 
northern MO/IA. Expect gusty southerly winds to develop through the 
mid and late mooring hours and continue through the afternoon hours. 
The WAA within the warm sector will help high temperatures to reach 
the upper 80s northeast to mid 90s west. The PBL will mix deeper 
across the western counties, thus surface dewpoints wil mix out into 
the mid to upper 60s during the afternoon hours. Eastern KS should 
keep lower 70 dewpoints. Maximum heat indices will be in the upper 
90s to near 103 across the eastern counties of the CWA. Heat indices 
will be a bit lower across north central KS with mid 90s to around 
100 degrees. Since maximum heat induces will remain below 103 
degrees, I will not issue a heat advisories, but it will feel hot and
humid for this time of year.

As the H5 trough lifts northeast across the central High Plains into 
the northern Plains late this afternoon, a surface cold front will 
move east across west central KS. Thunderstorms will develop along 
this front from eastern NE, southwest into north central KS, then 
southwest into southwest KS. The higher instability and effective 
shear values will be located across eastern NE/western IA where there 
will be a better chance for supercell thunderstorms to develop, 
which could produce all hazards. Farther southwest along the front 
the instability will be less, with MLCAPES in the 1000-2000 J/KG 
range. Forecast soundings show inverted V profiles, so any 
thunderstorm that develops in this environment late this afternoon 
may produce strong downdrafts. Effective shear will be 25 to 35 KTS, 
thus any organized updraft that develops with mid level rotation may
produce large hail along with the damaging wind gusts. The strong to
sever thunderstorms will move into the western counties during the 
late afternoon and evening hours. After sunset the line of storms 
may weaken a bit but the front should slowly shift southeast through 
the night. If thunderstorms train along the front during the evening 
and overnight hours there may be some localized flooding. PWs across 
north central KS will in the 1.5-2.0" range.


Tuesday, the H5 trough will lift from the northern Plains Monday 
night into Ontario Canada by Tuesday afternoon. The strong 
southwesterly H5 jet will lift northeast of the area.  The surface 
front will shift southeast across the CWA and most CAMs and CPMs 
forecast the front along a LWC to EMP line. Ahead of the front 
MLCAPE will be in the 1500-3000 J/kg range and effected shear will be
20 to 35 KTS. The environment Tuesday afternoon will be sufficient 
for strong to severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts and half 
dollar size hail. There will be elevated storms northwest of the 
front but MUCAPE values will be less than 500 J/KG, so if there is 
any hail it should be small. Most numerical models show a fairly 
progressive front, pushing southeast of the CWA after 00Z. I'm not 
sure how much training of thunderstorms will occur Tuesday afternoon 
if the front is progressing to the southeast.

Tuesday night through Wednesday:

The surface front will stall out just south of the CWA and the 
retreat northward as a warm front. Elevated thunderstorms will 
develop north of the front and continue into the morning hours as the
front lifts northeast across the CWA. By Wednesday afternoon the 
front will be along the NE border. There may be prolong period of 
heavy rainfall Tuesday night into Tuesday morning as a 40 to 50 KT
LLJ develops and advects 14 deg C dewpoints at 850mb northward 
across eastern KS. Some of these elevated storms may be strong to 
severe and producing hail up to 1.5". Also, PWs will be over 2.0", so
any areas with prolong heavy rainfall may see localize flooding.
